verses.1: Abimelech, son of Jerubbaal, went to his brothers and spoke with them. He also spoke to all the members of his father’s family.
verses.2: Speak to me, O leaders of Shechem! What is good for you? Who rules over you? Seventy men, all of them sons of Jerubbaal. If only one man could rule over you, and you would remember me as your ruler, just like I am in your hearts and among your people.
verses.3: And the men of Imo spoke to him in the ears of all the men of Shechem about all these things. They were filled with sorrow because of Abimelech, for they said, “Our brother is he.”
verses.4: And they gave him seventy pieces of silver from the house of Laban. With those coins, Abimelech hired men who were ruthless and violent. And they went after him.
verses.5: And Abi’ah came into his father’s house. He killed his brothers, the seventy men of Jebus. He also spared Yotham, the youngest son of Jebus, because he was a child.
verses.6: And all the leaders of Shechem, and all the houses of Milo, gathered together. They went and made Abimelech king over them, in a situation that was favorable for him in Shechem.
verses.7: And they cried out to them. He went and stood at the top of Mount Gerizim. Then he cried out loudly and said to them, “Hear me, rulers of Shechem! May God hear you too.”
verses.8: The trees went away to be carved by a king. They said to the king, “Your Majesty, please rule over us.”
verses.9: And he said to them, “The tree has stopped producing its fruit. It no longer produces anything that can please God and people. So I went away and planted trees instead.”
verses.10: And the trees said to Tena, “You are our king over us.”
verses.11: And she said to them, “I have stopped my mourning for my husband and my sorrow. I have gone on my way, along with the other women.”
verses.12: And the trees said to the fig tree, “You shall be our king over us.”
verses.13: And she said to them, “The vineyard of my master has been destroyed. God and people have abandoned it. I went over to the trees.”
verses.14: And all the trees said to the gardener, “Go, you who are our king.”
verses.15: And the Atad said to the trees, “Is it true that you want to make me king over you? Then come under my protection. But if you do not do so, fire will come from the Atad and burn up your branches.”
verses.16: And now, if indeed and sincerely you have done these things, and if you have appointed Abimelech as king over them. And if it’s well done, then with Joram and his family, and if they are willing to cooperate with him, then you can do this.
verses.17: My father fought against you, and he threw his soul away from you. He also defeated you by force.
verses.18: And today, you stood in the house of my father. You killed seventy of his sons on one stone. Then you made Abimelech, his son, king over the people of Shechem. For he is our brother.
verses.19: And if, in truth and forever, you have done these things with Yerubal and his house today, then rejoice in Abimelach. And he too will rejoice with you.
verses.20: And if fire comes out from Abimelech, and it consumes the men of Shechem and the house of Milo, then fire will also come out from the men of Shechem and from the house of Milo, and it will consume Abimelech.
verses.21: And Yotam ran away. He went into the wilderness and settled there, behind Abimelech, his brother’s house.
verses.22: And Abimelech ruled over Israel for three years.
verses.23: And God sent a evil spirit among Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem. The leaders of Shechem became unfaithful to Abimelech.
verses.24: Let the blood of seventy sons of Jirubal be poured out upon Abimelech, their enemy who killed them. And let the blood of the leaders of Shechem also be poured out upon them, as they strengthened their hands to kill their own brothers.
verses.25: And the men of Shechem laid siege to him on the mountains. They took away everything that passed through their way. Then they reported this to Abimelech.
verses.26: And Gaal, the son of Ehud, and his brothers came and passed through Shechem. They made their home there.
verses.27: And they went out into the field, plowed their fields. Then they went back home, ate, drank, and cursed Abimelech.
verses.28: And Gaal, son of Esau, said, “Who are these people from Midian and Shechem? They served us even when they were still children. Zebul was their leader. They served the people of Hamor from Shechem. How can we possibly serve them?”
verses.29: And who will give this people into my hands and release Abimelech? He said to Abimelech, “May your army and your people go away.”
verses.30: And Zebul, the chief of the city, heard what Gilead son of Abed said. So he became angry.
verses.31: And he sent demons to Abimelech, secretly, with the words: “Look, Gaal, the son of Ehud, and his brothers have come. They are causing trouble in your city.”
verses.32: And now, let there be light at night, you and the people who are with you. Let them go forth into the field.
verses.33: And in the morning, when the sun began to shine, you will spread out your tent over the city. Then you will see him and the people who came to you. And you will do to them whatever it is your hand can do.
verses.34: And Abimelech and all the people with him rose up in the night. They lay down on their beds, four in each group.
verses.35: And Gilead, the son of a servant, went out and stood at the gate of the city. Abimelech and the people who were with him rushed forward.
verses.36: And God saw the people, and He said to Zebul: “Look! The people are coming down from the mountains.” And He said to him, “Zebul, you see these people as mere human beings.”
verses.37: And Gaal continued to speak. He said, “Look! People are coming from the land of Tabor. One of them is coming along the road from Elon Me’unanim.”
verses.38: And Zebul said to him, “Who is your father, who says, ‘Who can defeat me?’ For this people has already rebelled against me. Now go away from them and fight against them!”
verses.39: And Gilead went out before the rulers of Shechem, and he fought against Abimelech.
verses.40: Abimelech pursued him, and he ran away from him. Many people fell to the ground at the entrance of the gate.
verses.41: And Abimelech settled in Arumah. He drove Zebul and his brothers out of their home in Shechem.
verses.42: And in the evening, the people went out and reported to Abimelech.
verses.43: And he took the people and divided them into three groups. Then he went into the field. Suddenly, he saw that the people were coming out of the city. He then rushed towards them and attacked them.
verses.44: And Abimelech and the leaders who were with him went out to stand at the gate of the city. The two leaders went out and searched every one of those in the field; they killed them all.
verses.45: And Abimelech fought against the city all day long. He conquered the city and its people, killing everyone inside. Then he destroyed the city and sowed terror among its inhabitants.
verses.46: And all the rulers of Megidda heard this, and they came to the house of El in Beth-El.
verses.47: And he told Abimelech that all the leaders of Magdad had been defeated.
verses.48: Abimelech climbed the mountain of Tzalmon. All the people who were with him also went up there. Abimelech took the axes in his hands, cut down some trees, and placed them on the ground. Then he said to the people who were with him, “What have you seen? What have I done? Do as I have done.”
verses.49: And all the people also chose a leader. They followed Abimelech, and they set fire to the city. All the people from Megiddo died; there were thousands of men and women who died in that fire.
verses.50: And Abimelech went to Tebek. He lay down in Tebek and captured her.
verses.51: And from the hill stood out, within the city. All the men and women of the city rushed up there together. They closed their doors behind them and stood on the top of the hill.
verses.52: Abimelech came to the tower and fought against it. He then advanced to the entrance of the tower, and set it on fire with fire.
verses.53: And one woman threw a bundle of straw onto Abimelech’s head. Then she ran away.
verses.54: And he quickly called out to the boy, “Take away all his possessions!” He said to him, “Smash your house down and destroy it, so that no one will say that I killed him.” But the boy killed him.
verses.55: And the Israelites saw that Abimelech was dead. So they went to his place.
verses.56: And God punished Abimelech for the evil he did to his father, who killed his seventy sons.
verses.57: And all the evil deeds of the people of Shechem were returned to them by God. Then came the curse from Yotam son of Yerubal upon them.
